Subject: Intro demo with Redwood — June 21?

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro last week — we’d love to see Redwood in action. Are you available for a 60–90 minute intro/demo on Monday, June 21 or Tuesday, June 22? Our team will include two product folks and one engineer (see cc).

High-level ask: a product demo focused on latency and cost controls for inference, plus a quick walkthrough of the Dedicated offering. If possible, please include a short appendix on Private (VPC) deployment options.

Attached: corporate deck (internal context).

Available windows (ET):
- Mon 6/21: 10:00–12:00 or 15:00–17:00
- Tue 6/22: 09:00–11:00

If those don’t work, we can be flexible — looking to lock something this week.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Miller
Director of Product, Quark Health
[jordan.miller@quarkhealth.ai]

Hi Jordan — thanks for the context and the deck. Vivek here (solutions partnerships). Quick note: our typical "intro" demo is fine, but based on what you mentioned (engineer attending + interest in Dedicated/Private), the team actually suggests converting this into a compact engineering lab — hands-on, focused on real latency/cost tradeoffs and a short run of the SDK + model selection. That tends to surface the right questions for a POC faster than a slide-heavy session.

Two narrow options from our side:
- Option A: Mon June 27, 14:00–15:00 ET — compact engineering lab (60 min)
- Option B: Wed June 29, 11:00–12:00 ET — compact engineering lab (60 min)

If you confirm one of those, Laura (solutions engineer) will prep a 15-min environment checklist and Marissa (CS lead) will send a short pre-read. To make the lab effective we’ll need:
- One engineer with SSH access to a dev VM or temporary AWS role OR a small sample dataset + sample prompts
- A short list of two target models or use cases you want us to run (e.g., reranking + generation)

If these dates are a non-starter we can keep to the June 21/22 windows and do a lighter product demo instead.

Thanks — I’ll hold Option A tentatively until I hear back.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com]

Perfect — Tue June 30, 11:00–12:00 ET works for us. We’ll switch the session to a "Compact Engineering Lab" (60 minutes). Below is the confirmed plan and a short checklist to maximize value. I’ll follow up with the calendar invite and the runbook link.

Confirmed attendees (so far):
- Jordan Miller — Quark Health (product)
- Sanjay Patel — Quark Health (engineering)
- Vivek Kulkarni — Redwood (solutions partnerships)
- Laura Bennett — Redwood (solutions engineer)
- Marissa Cole — Redwood (customer success)

Agenda (60 min):
1) 5 min — quick goals check (what success looks like)
2) 15 min — environment & onboarding (we’ll pull a couple of prompts / sample payloads)
3) 30 min — hands-on runs across two candidate models (latency/cost tradeoffs + simple KV cache demo)
4) 10 min — next steps & POC scoping (roles, timelines, required artifacts)

Pre-lab checklist (please complete before Tue 30):
- Provide one SSH key or temporary IAM role for a lightweight dev sandbox OR upload a 10–50 MB sample payload to a shared Drive link
- Share two target use cases or prompts (short list)
- Confirm whether you prefer Hosted API demo or a quick run on a Dedicated test node (we can provision a short-lived node if you want realistic throughput numbers)

Attachments & links:
- Compact runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=compact-lab-runbook (we attached a local copy too)
- Placeholder calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=example-compact-lab
- Attachment: compact-lab-runbook.md (runbook, 3 pages)

Notes on procurement / next steps: if the lab surfaces a POC, we can follow up with a mutual action plan and draft MSA/redline guidance. Marissa will circle back on typical timelines and cost expectations after the session.

See you on the 30th — I’ll send the invite and runbook to the group by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
